claims.text: Each version has its own controller and DTOs because the controller's route decides the URL and the DTO decides the JSON shape; keeping the business rules in the shared service means they exist once.
claims.source_hint: outline item 3; comment in V2/OrdersV2Controller.cs lines 9-12 at stage-2

claims.text: The version in the URL names a version of the whole API, not of one resource or record: /api/v2/orders/5 is order 5 read through version 2. A version need not repeat every endpoint; Đơn Hàng's v2 has two.

Only a breaking change needs a new version; each version kept is code to run, test and fix, so a team usually retires an old version once its clients have moved, removing it only after a date announced to them.
claims.source_hint: outline items 4 and misconceptions of backend.l2.api-versioning

claims.text: Removing /api/v1 would itself be a breaking change for every client still calling it, including the Flutter app's product and order pages.

claims.text: Caddy at stage-2 forwards /api/v2/* to the API container, as it does /api/v1/*.
In ASP.NET Core, an [Authorize] endpoint reached without credentials answers 401 when the default authentication scheme is JWT bearer, while a path that matches no endpoint answers 404.
